# Orlando's Claude Code setup: every page in one file

> The AI Setup section of this blog, every page's plain copy in the order of its main page. AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs.

# AI Setup

- Kind: Claude Code setup
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/.

A tour of Orlando's personal AI setup: how it's organized, rules, skills, agents, apps, and settings.

## What this is

This section is for people, and their agents, who want to borrow from a working AI setup. Every text here can be copied and adapted.

It is one person's setup, Orlando's, built around Claude Code on a Mac. It is not a product.

It changes often. Every page says when its own content last changed.

The diagram as text:

- How Orlando's AI setup fits together.
- Orlando chats with a Claude Code session from the Mac or his phone.
- Orlando uses his apps: Corillo (review documents with an agent), Brega (a to-do list shared with agents), Pregón (publish a post), and Latido (a window onto the heartbeat).
- Corillo and Brega pass comments, edits, and tasks to a session and back.
- While Orlando is away, the Heartbeat (jobs on a timer) and the Relay (a roadmap, one fresh session per batch) start sessions.
- A session reads the rules at the start: global, workspace, and project.
- Settings and hooks check each step a session takes.
- A session can use 14 skills: close-shop, save-session, process-feedback, tune-setup, connect, obsidian-to-hugo, publish-prep, publish-post, publish-setup, podcast, video-title-cards, relay, heartbeat, and rex.
- A session can work as one of 3 custom agents: writer, trainer, and financial advisor.
- A session reads and writes the files on the Mac: the knowledge base (an Obsidian vault), projects (by area, in dated folders), tools (finished and reusable), and scratch (throwaway files).
- The files are kept under local version history and backed up to the cloud.

## The pieces

- [How it's organized](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/workspace/): the workspace's folders, the knowledge base's shape, version history, backups, and how Python scripts run.
- [Rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/): the rules every session starts from (3 rules files).
- [Skills](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/): written routines a session can run (14 skills).
- [Custom agents](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/): roles a session can take, each with its own prompt (3 agents).
- [Apps](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/apps/): the apps around the sessions, described (6 apps).
- [Settings and hooks](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/settings/): the switches underneath (2 hooks).

Orlando's weekly AI digest is public too, as the [Newsletter](https://oneillo.com/newsletter/).

## How this section is made

1. Orlando starts a publish when he wants one.
2. The run gathers his rules, skills, and agents from his Mac, from a fixed list of places.
3. An AI model takes out anything private and writes the short descriptions.
4. A separate check holds back any page where something private is left: that page is shown as described only, or left out until the next publish.
5. The pages are built. At first Orlando looks at what changed and says yes before it goes live.

Nobody edits these pages by hand. A description may be wrong where the text under it is right: the text is the source.

## Borrowing from it

- Every text has a copy button.
- Placeholders look like `<brokerage>` or `<project-folder>`. Put your own in their place.
- You can hand a page's address to your own agent and ask it to adapt the page to your setup.

## Pages

- [How it's organized](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/workspace/index.md): How Orlando's AI workspace is organized: its folders, the knowledge base, version history, backups, and Python scripts.
- [Rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/index.md): The rules files in Orlando's AI setup, the instructions every session starts from.
- [Skills](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/index.md): The skills in Orlando's AI setup, the written routines a session can run.
- [Custom agents](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/index.md): The custom agents in Orlando's AI setup, the roles a session can take.
- [Apps](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/apps/index.md): The apps around Orlando's AI sessions, each described in a few lines.
- [Settings and hooks](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/settings/index.md): The settings and hooks in Orlando's AI setup, described by kind.

# How it's organized

- Kind: Claude Code workspace
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/workspace/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/workspace/.

How Orlando's AI workspace is organized: its folders, the knowledge base, version history, backups, and Python scripts.

This page explains how Orlando's setup is organized: one workspace for agents, a knowledge base, local git history, an automatic cloud backup, and Python scripts that carry their own needs.

## The workspace

One folder holds everything. It has the knowledge base, projects sorted by area in dated folders that each have a context file, finished tools, and a scratch folder. The scratch folder is swept daily and never holds anything vital.

## The knowledge base

The knowledge base is a vault of notes. It is split into areas, and each area has a hub note. Concept notes link back to their sources. A scratch folder holds notes for Orlando to review. Agents start from the vault's rules file and its index. When a project closes, the lasting facts move into the knowledge base.

## Version history with git

The workspace, the Claude Code config folder, and the vault are each a local git repo with no remote. Agents do all the git work. There is a commit at the end of each session and a checkpoint before a bulk change. Undoing means restoring files. Why: any change an agent makes can be seen and undone.

## Backups

"If an agent ever accidentally removes a file completely, I can generally recover it from the cloud storage's recycle bin online."

The backup is one of three safety nets:

1. Deletes go to the Trash, so a mistake can be recovered from there.
2. Local version history keeps every committed change.
3. The cloud copy mirrors the workspace and the Claude Code config folder.

His backup goes to OneDrive (cloud storage). It copies `~/ai/` and `~/.claude/` every 30 minutes, on a timer. A private GitHub repo or similar is another way to do it, with one catch: it has no recycle bin for a file deleted between commits, so it needs frequent automatic commits.

To restore, follow these steps:

1. Sign in to the cloud storage on the new computer and let the backup folder download fully.
2. Install the tools the setup needs, such as Claude Code and uv.
3. Copy the backed-up folders back to `~/ai/` and `~/.claude/`, without deleting anything.
4. Check that every git repo answers and still has its history.
5. Do a dry run of the backup to see what it would delete, and stop if the list is long.
6. Turn the backup timer back on last, so it never mirrors a half-restored computer over the backup.

## Python with uv

Every script runs with `uv run` and declares its Python version and packages at its top. There are no virtual environments and no `pip`. Why: a script carries what it needs, nothing is installed system-wide, there is nothing to set up or clean up, and an agent can write and run a one-off script safely.

```
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.12"
# dependencies = ["requests"]
# ///
```

**Works with:** [Brega](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/apps/#brega), [Close shop](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/close-shop/), [Corillo](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/apps/#corillo), [Financial advisor](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/financial-advisor/), [Heartbeat](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/heartbeat/), [Process feedback](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/process-feedback/), [Rex](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/rex/), [Save session](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/save-session/), [Trainer](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/trainer/), [Tune setup](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/tune-setup/), and [Writer](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/writer/).

The same rules appear as text on the [Global rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/global/) and [Workspace rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/workspace/) pages.

# Rules

- Kind: Claude Code rules files
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/.

The rules files in Orlando's AI setup, the instructions every session starts from.

Rules come in layers. The global rules apply to every session, anywhere on the Mac. The workspace rules apply in the agent workspace, the folder where agents do their work. The knowledge base has its own rules file, for agents working in the notes.

- [Global rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/global/): Sets global rules for every session: direct style, keeping the Mac awake, file defaults, cleanup, Python with uv, and formatting.
- [Workspace rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/workspace/): Sets the shared rules for every session in a workspace: how to work together, where files live, how projects start, and how history is kept.
- [Knowledge base rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/knowledge-base/): Sets the rules agents follow to find, write, link, and check notes in a knowledge base kept as a vault of Markdown notes.

## Project rules and context files

Each project adds its own rules file, and a context file that holds the project's goal, constraints, and decisions. A session reads them before it starts, so it can pick up where the last one stopped. They hold each project's private detail, so their text is not shared here.

## Memory

Claude Code keeps a memory for the workspace and one for each custom agent: lessons learned while working, and where things are. Memory is private by nature. It is never read for this section, and nothing here comes from it.

## Pages

- [Global rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/global/index.md): Sets global rules for every session: direct style, keeping the Mac awake, file defaults, cleanup, Python with uv, and formatting.
- [Workspace rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/workspace/index.md): Sets the shared rules for every session in a workspace: how to work together, where files live, how projects start, and how history is kept.
- [Knowledge base rules](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/knowledge-base/index.md): Sets the rules agents follow to find, write, link, and check notes in a knowledge base kept as a vault of Markdown notes.

# Global rules

- Kind: Claude Code rules file
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/global/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/global/.

Sets global rules for every session: direct style, keeping the Mac awake, file defaults, cleanup, Python with uv, and formatting.

- **What it is:** Global Steering is a Claude Code global rules file that sets how every session and agent talks, handles files, cleans up, and runs Python.
- **How it starts:** Every Claude Code session reads it at the start.
- **Where the file goes:** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- **Needs:** uv, Rex, and macOS

**Works with:** [Rex](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/rex/).

## The rules file (`CLAUDE.md`)

The global rules file read by every Claude Code session and agent, covering style, keeping the Mac awake, file naming, cleanup, Python scripts, and formatting.

````
# Global Steering

These rules apply to all Claude Code sessions and agents.

## Interaction Style

- Be direct. Lead with the answer or action, not the reasoning.
- Skip preamble, filler phrases, and trailing summaries. If I can read the diff, don't restate it.
- No compliment sandwiches. If something is wrong, say so clearly.
- Use plain language. Explain things like a smart colleague, not a textbook.

## Keeping the Mac Awake

- When I say I'm stepping away, when I work with you over Remote Control, or when a job runs unattended, keep the Mac awake without being asked. Wrap the long job (`caffeinate -ims <command>` lasts exactly as long as it runs), or start one `caffeinate -ims -t <seconds>` in the background sized to the work, unless one is already running. The display may sleep: Remote Control doesn't need it. Stop only what you started.
- While the front desk (`~/ai/tools/scripts/front-desk.sh`, in its own Rex tab) runs, it already keeps the Mac awake: start nothing more.
- When I step away and the session isn't on Remote Control, suggest `/remote-control`. While it is, send a push notification when work is ready for my feedback or blocked on me, and each time a reply ends with a question for me. Never for routine progress.

## File Defaults

- Unless I ask otherwise, create files in markdown format.
- Use descriptive, lowercase, hyphenated filenames (e.g., `my-topic-notes.md`).

## Filesystem Boundaries

- Read and write within `~/ai/` and `~/.claude/` only, unless I explicitly direct you elsewhere.
- Do not create files outside these directories without asking first.

## Cleaning Up

- Clean up after yourself, and brief every agent you start to do the same. Whatever a task creates that isn't the deliverable (temp folders, test data, caches, builds, downloads, worktrees, background processes) is removed when the task ends. Tests remove what they create as they finish.
- Leftovers that grow with use are a leak, the same as a memory leak in an app. This covers the system temp folder (`$TMPDIR`), not just the project folder.
- Before long, repeated or parallel runs, check what each run leaves behind and where, check free disk space (`df -h`), and put a cleanup or cap in place. Check free space again at milestones.

## Python

- Use `uv run` to execute Python scripts. Do not create virtual environments or use pip directly.
- Always include inline script metadata declaring dependencies and Python version:
  ```
  # /// script
  # requires-python = ">=3.12"
  # dependencies = ["requests"]
  # ///
  ```
- Omit the `dependencies` field if the script only uses the standard library.

## Formatting

- Prefer short, direct sentences.
- Use headers and lists to organize multi-part responses, but don't over-structure short answers.
- No emojis unless I ask for them.
- Use commas, periods, colons, or parentheses where an em dash might go. Em dashes read as AI-written, in chat and in files.
````

# Workspace rules

- Kind: Claude Code rules file
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/workspace/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/workspace/.

Sets the shared rules for every session in a workspace: how to work together, where files live, how projects start, and how history is kept.

- **What it is:** The workspace rules file is a Claude Code rules file that sets how agents work with Orlando, where things live in the workspace, how projects start, and how git history is kept.
- **How it starts:** Every Claude Code session started in the workspace, or in a folder inside it, reads it at the start.
- **Where the file goes:** `<your-workspace>/CLAUDE.md`
- **Needs:** Nothing extra
- **Taken out for privacy:** 5 money or health area names, 2 backup arrangements, and 2 generalized examples.

**Works with:** [Close shop](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/close-shop/), [Corillo](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/apps/#corillo), [Financial advisor](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/financial-advisor/), [Heartbeat](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/heartbeat/), [Process feedback](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/process-feedback/), [Save session](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/save-session/), [Trainer](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/trainer/), [Tune setup](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/tune-setup/), and [Writer](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/writer/).

## The rules file (`CLAUDE.md`)

The rules file every session in the workspace loads, covering how agents should work with Orlando, the folder layout, how projects start or resume, version history, and where feedback and memory go.

```
# Shared Agent Guidelines

These apply to every session in ~/ai/, including the custom agents (`writer`, `trainer`, `financial-advisor`) defined in `~/.claude/agents/`.

## How to Work With Me

- Push back when you think I'm wrong. Don't agree just to be agreeable. If I'm proposing something that doesn't make sense, say so directly with your reasoning before executing. The same goes for what's already in place: if part of the setup no longer earns its keep, say so.
- Keep the setup simple. I want the best results for the least complexity. Every rule, skill, file and automation must earn its place; propose removing things as readily as adding them. Models and tools improve fast, so treat past setup decisions as provisional.
- If you don't know something, say so. Never fill gaps with plausible-sounding guesses. Getting it wrong is worse than admitting uncertainty.
- Don't state quantitative claims, technical judgments, or narrative details as fact unless you can verify them from available data. If you're uncertain, say what you observe and let me confirm.
- When context files are loaded at session start, mine them for constraints and existing patterns before proposing or asking. Don't ask questions already answered by the data.
- Use parallel subagents for independent research or reviews across several areas. Do small lookups yourself.
- Anything you want me to review (a plan, a draft, findings) opens in Corillo by default, not as a file path or pasted in chat. When I'm on my phone over Remote Control, don't open or create documents in Corillo: I'm not at the computer, so it doesn't help. Share Markdown I should read by copying it into `knowledge-base/_scratch/`, as the "Scratch" part of `knowledge-base/AGENTS.md` says. I read it in Obsidian and type my feedback at the bottom. At the Mac, review stays in Corillo.
- `~/ai` is my agent workspace. Inside it, do what the work needs without asking me first. That includes answering Claude Code's "trust this folder" question for a folder you made here yourself. Bring me in when something reaches outside this folder (`~/.claude` stays as my global instructions say). The rules a project sets for itself, such as clean-room fences, still hold, and so do the ask-first lines in this file (a new area under `projects/`, leftover edits another session may own).

## Workspace Layout

- `knowledge-base/`: Orlando's durable knowledge, a link to his Obsidian vault, organized by area. Before reading or writing there, follow `knowledge-base/AGENTS.md`; start from `knowledge-base/index.md` and the area hubs. Read what the task needs; don't preload. Project-specific, short-lived context stays in the project folder; at `/close-shop`, anything a project produced that will stay true moves into the knowledge base.
- `projects/<area>/`: working output by area (for example `blog/`, `ai-setup/`, and `misc/`). Dated subfolders (`yyyymmdd-slug/`) for discrete pieces of work. When a project is finished, move it into a `zzCompleted/` folder inside its own area (e.g. `projects/<area>/zzCompleted/`), keeping its folder name. File by subject: a project that builds a tool goes in the area the tool serves, and once the tool is in regular use it moves to top-level `tools/`, and keeps being improved there. `misc/` is the fallback for projects that fit no other area. Keep this level small and intentional: don't add an area without asking Orlando, and nest deeper rather than spreading out.
- `tools/`: finished, reusable tools for the AI setup. Standalone scripts go in `tools/scripts/` (e.g. `shrink-video.sh`). Larger tools get their own subfolder (e.g. a backup tool that runs on a timer and has a restore runbook); a tool with its own git repo must be listed in `.gitignore` so the workspace repo doesn't absorb it.
- `tmp/`: scratch space for throwaway files (intermediate outputs, test conversions, downloads you only need briefly). Ephemeral, not committed, not backed up. Use it instead of a project folder or the system temp dir for anything that isn't a deliverable. Anything there can be deleted at any time: a daily heartbeat job (`sweep-scratch`) removes what is untouched for 7 days, the vault's `_scratch/` too. Never keep anything vital in either; originals live in project folders.

## Starting or Resuming a Project

When Orlando says we're working on a project that already has a folder, your first action, before any other reading or work, is to check for a `context.md` at the folder's root and read it if it exists. It holds that project's goal, constraints and decisions.

When Orlando says we're working on a project and no folder for it exists, create one at `projects/<area>/yyyymmdd-slug/` (today's date, short hyphenated slug) before producing output. Pick the area that fits the work; use `misc/` if none does. Check for an existing folder first (including the area's `zzCompleted/`) so you don't duplicate one. Tell Orlando the path you created.

Every project folder gets a `context.md` at its root, created with the folder. Use the format in the `save-session` skill (`~/.claude/skills/save-session/SKILL.md`) and fill in what's known at the start: the goal, constraints, and first steps. When Orlando sets a constraint or makes a decision, add it to `context.md` right away so it survives compaction; `/save-session` does the full update at the end of a session.

## Version History

- The workspace, the Claude Code config (agents, skills, memory) and the knowledge base each keep a local git history. Agents handle git; Orlando never runs it.
- Commit at `/close-shop`: this session's changes first, then leftover edits once Orlando confirms no other session is working on them.
- Before a bulk change (moving, renaming, or deleting many files, or rewriting several config files at once), commit the current state as a checkpoint first so it can be undone in one step.
- These three stay local: never push them. A repo with its own remote is pushed only when I ask or one of my skills says so. Rewrite history only when I ask. Keep keys and passwords out of every commit. To undo something, confirm with Orlando, then restore the specific files rather than resetting the repo.
- Delete with `trash`, not `rm`, so a mistake can be recovered from the Trash (`rm` is fine inside `tmp/`). Before deleting something you didn't create, check that nothing references it.

## Feedback and Memory

- Corrections go to auto memory as `feedback` memories, not to a separate log. `/process-feedback` reviews them at each `/tune-setup`.
- Bugs and ideas for my apps and tools go in a `feedback.md` at the root of that app's or tool's folder (for example `tools/corillo/feedback.md`), the moment I mention one: newest first, the date, what I saw or want in my words, what I was doing, and a status (open, in batch N, done in build X). Make the file with the first item. The next batch or session for that app takes its work from there and marks what it built. This is separate from feedback memories, which are about how you work with me.
- Memory, the workspace's and each agent's, holds lessons on how to work with me, where things are, and what was decided. What is true about me (profile, plans, and the like) goes in the knowledge base, with at most a one-line pointer in memory. An agent that finds such a fact in its memory offers to move it, with my OK, at its next real session with me.
```

- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/rules/knowledge-base/.

Sets the rules agents follow to find, write, link, and check notes in a knowledge base kept as a vault of Markdown notes.

- **What it is:** The knowledge base's rules file is a Claude Code rules file that tells agents where to start, how to name, write, and link notes, where drafts for review go, and how history is kept.
- **How it starts:** Sessions read it before they work in the knowledge base.
- **Needs:** Obsidian, uv, and git

Described only: its text is not shared.

# Skills

- Kind: Claude Code skills
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/
- Last updated: 2026-11-23

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/.

The skills in Orlando's AI setup, the written routines a session can run.

A skill is a written routine. Orlando starts one with a slash, or Claude picks it up when it fits.

## Ending a session well

- [Close shop](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/close-shop/): Ends a working session in three steps: saves project context, checks corrections are in memory, and commits the session's changes.
- [Process feedback](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/process-feedback/): Reviews saved memories, promotes lasting lessons to the right place, and prunes the rest so memory stays lean.
- [Save session](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/save-session/): Saves where a project stands in a context file so the next session can pick up where this one left off.
- [Tune setup](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/tune-setup/): Researches current Anthropic guidance, updates a guidance file, and proposes specific improvements to a Claude Code setup.

## Knowledge base

- [Connect](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/connect/): Links new knowledge base notes to concept notes, builds concept notes for recurring ideas, and adds cross-area links.

## Writing and publishing

- [Obsidian to Hugo](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/obsidian-to-hugo/): Converts an Obsidian blog post to Hugo-ready Markdown, fixes links and pictures, and places it in a review folder.
- [Publish post](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/publish-post/): Publishes a finished blog post to a Hugo site, checks the build, and pushes it to GitHub.
- [Publish prep](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/publish-prep/): Prepares a finished blog post for publishing with title options, a description, a LinkedIn blurb, and a Substack version.
- [Publish setup](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/publish-setup/): Publishes an AI setup to a blog section: gathers files, has agents remove private details, checks twice, previews, and asks before going live.

## Audio and video

- [Podcast](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/podcast/): Turns source documents into a two-host podcast-style MP3 by writing a script, then rendering it locally with a text-to-speech voice.
- [Video title cards](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/video-title-cards/): Makes intro, outro, and interstitial title cards with ffmpeg and joins them to screen recordings.

## Working while you are away

- [Heartbeat](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/heartbeat/): Adds, changes, pauses, or removes scheduled jobs on the heartbeat, a scheduler that runs a free check and then an agent session with limits.
- [Relay](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/relay/): Runs a project's roadmap unattended as a relay of fresh Claude Code sessions, each leading one batch with parallel agents and handing off to the next.

## From others

- [Rex](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/rex/): Manages Rex sessions, tabs, and panes, runs commands, and reads terminal output from the command line.

## Pages

- [Close shop](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/close-shop/index.md): Ends a working session in three steps: saves project context, checks corrections are in memory, and commits the session's changes.
- [Process feedback](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/process-feedback/index.md): Reviews saved memories, promotes lasting lessons to the right place, and prunes the rest so memory stays lean.
- [Save session](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/save-session/index.md): Saves where a project stands in a context file so the next session can pick up where this one left off.
- [Tune setup](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/tune-setup/index.md): Researches current Anthropic guidance, updates a guidance file, and proposes specific improvements to a Claude Code setup.
- [Connect](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/connect/index.md): Links new knowledge base notes to concept notes, builds concept notes for recurring ideas, and adds cross-area links.
- [Obsidian to Hugo](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/obsidian-to-hugo/index.md): Converts an Obsidian blog post to Hugo-ready Markdown, fixes links and pictures, and places it in a review folder.
- [Publish post](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/publish-post/index.md): Publishes a finished blog post to a Hugo site, checks the build, and pushes it to GitHub.
- [Publish prep](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/publish-prep/index.md): Prepares a finished blog post for publishing with title options, a description, a LinkedIn blurb, and a Substack version.
- [Publish setup](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/publish-setup/index.md): Publishes an AI setup to a blog section: gathers files, has agents remove private details, checks twice, previews, and asks before going live.
- [Podcast](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/podcast/index.md): Turns source documents into a two-host podcast-style MP3 by writing a script, then rendering it locally with a text-to-speech voice.
- [Video title cards](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/video-title-cards/index.md): Makes intro, outro, and interstitial title cards with ffmpeg and joins them to screen recordings.
- [Heartbeat](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/heartbeat/index.md): Adds, changes, pauses, or removes scheduled jobs on the heartbeat, a scheduler that runs a free check and then an agent session with limits.
- [Relay](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/relay/index.md): Runs a project's roadmap unattended as a relay of fresh Claude Code sessions, each leading one batch with parallel agents and handing off to the next.
- [Rex](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/rex/index.md): Manages Rex sessions, tabs, and panes, runs commands, and reads terminal output from the command line.

# Close shop

- Kind: Claude Code skill
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/close-shop/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/close-shop/.

Ends a working session in three steps: saves project context, checks corrections are in memory, and commits the session's changes.

- **What it is:** Close shop is a Claude Code skill that ends a working session by saving project context, checking memory, and committing changes.
- **How it starts:** You type `/close-shop`. Claude doesn't start it by itself.
- **Where the file goes:** `~/.claude/skills/close-shop/SKILL.md`
- **Needs:** git
- **To make it yours:** Put your own values where you see `<vault-history-folder>`.
  Taken out for privacy: 1 path.

**Works with:** [Connect](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/connect/), [Financial advisor](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/financial-advisor/), [Process feedback](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/process-feedback/), [Save session](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/save-session/), [Trainer](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/trainer/), [Tune setup](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/tune-setup/), and [Writer](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/writer/).

## The skill file (`SKILL.md`)

The skill's instructions for the end of a working session, covering saving project context, saving corrections to memory, and committing the session's changes to local git repos.

```
---
name: close-shop
description: End-of-session routine that saves project context, checks corrections are saved to memory, and commits this session's changes
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, AskUserQuestion
---

# Close Shop

Run the end-of-session routine in three steps, in order.

## Step 1: Save session

Save for each project the session changed: a folder under `~/ai/projects/`, a tool under `~/ai/tools/`, or any folder that already has a `context.md`. Skip if no project files were read, edited, or created, or the session was just conversation or brainstorming. If skipping, say why in one line and move on.

Otherwise, read `~/.claude/skills/save-session/SKILL.md` and follow it.

Then promote durable knowledge. If the project produced anything that will stay true after the project ends (facts about Orlando, reference material, finished notes), move it into the knowledge base at `~/ai/knowledge-base/` (copy only when the project still needs the file, and say so), following its `AGENTS.md`, and run `uv run ~/ai/tools/scripts/kb.py check` on what you added. Then note in `context.md` what moved and where it lives now. Then connect it: follow `~/.claude/skills/connect/SKILL.md` for the notes you added or changed, so they link to the concepts they discuss and new recurring ideas get concept notes. Say in one line what you moved and connected, or that nothing qualified.

## Step 2: Check corrections are in memory

Scan the session for moments Orlando corrected the approach, had to repeat himself, or confirmed a non-obvious approach worked. For each lesson that would change how an agent works in a future session, make sure auto memory has it as a `feedback` memory (in the session's memory directory, following the auto memory format), and save it if not. Skip one-off slips and anything already in a CLAUDE.md, agent file or memory. Say in one line what you saved, or that nothing qualified. `/process-feedback` reviews them at each `/tune-setup`.

## Step 3: Commit this session's changes

`~/ai/`, `~/.claude/`, and the knowledge base (`~/ai/knowledge-base/`, its history kept in `<vault-history-folder>`) are local git repos with no remote. Orlando never runs git; you do it.

For each of the three repos:

1. Run `git -C <repo> status --short`.
2. Stage only the files this session created, edited, or deleted, including the `context.md` and memory changes from Steps 1 and 2. Stage by explicit path (`git -C <repo> add -- <paths>`). Never `git add -A` or `git add .` at the repo root.
3. Commit only those paths (`git -C <repo> commit -m "<subject>" -- <paths>`), with a subject of `<agent>: <what changed>` (agent is `writer`, `trainer`, `financial-advisor`, or `main` for a plain session), under 72 characters. Add a short body with bullets for the main changes and the project folder, if any.
4. If nothing from this session changed in a repo, skip it.

If the session changed files in a folder that has its own repo (listed in `~/ai/.gitignore`), commit there by that repo's own rules, never with `git add -f` from `~/ai`, and name that repo in the closing line. If that repo's own rules say to ask about pushing, ask Orlando.

Then handle leftovers: changes this session didn't make. These are usually Orlando's own edits or another session's, and left alone they sit uncommitted for days. If any remain in any of the three, list them and ask Orlando once whether another session is still working on them. If not, add and commit them by explicit path (`-- <paths>`, as above) with the subject `unattributed: <short summary>`. If one is, leave those files alone.

Never push (the question above is the one exception), amend, rebase, reset, or otherwise rewrite history. Never commit secrets; if a file looks like one, stop and ask.

Finish by telling Orlando, in one line per repo, what was committed (or that nothing was), plus anything left uncommitted and why.
```

# Process feedback

- Kind: Claude Code skill
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/process-feedback/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/process-feedback/.

Reviews saved memories, promotes lasting lessons to the right place, and prunes the rest so memory stays lean.

- **What it is:** Process feedback is a Claude Code skill that reviews saved memories, moves lasting lessons to the right rules file, agent, skill, or hook, and deletes the rest.
- **How it starts:** You type `/process-feedback`. Claude doesn't start it by itself.
- **Where the file goes:** `~/.claude/skills/process-feedback/SKILL.md`
- **Needs:** Nothing extra
- **To make it yours:** Put your own values where you see `<workspace-project>`.
  Taken out for privacy: 1 path.

**Works with:** [Tune setup](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/tune-setup/).

## The skill file (`SKILL.md`)

The instructions for reviewing every saved memory and deciding whether to keep, promote, merge, or delete each one, run as part of a regular setup tune-up or on request.

```
---
name: process-feedback
description: Review memories, promote lasting lessons to the right place, and prune the rest so memory stays lean
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, AskUserQuestion
---

Claude Code's auto memory captures corrections as `feedback` memories, and they take effect in the next session on their own. This review keeps them from piling up: every memory index line loads in every session. It runs as part of each `/tune-setup`, or when Orlando asks.

Read every memory file, of every type (`user`, `feedback`, `project`, `reference`), and its index entry in:

- `~/.claude/projects/<workspace-project>/memory/` (workspace memory, loads in every `~/ai` session)
- `~/.claude/agent-memory/<name>/` for each agent (loads for that agent)

If there are none, say so and stop.

For each one, decide on one action:
- **Keep as memory** if it's a preference or lesson that's working where it is.
- **Promote to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`** if it applies to all work everywhere.
- **Promote to `~/ai/CLAUDE.md`** if it applies to every agent in the workspace.
- **Promote to an agent definition** (`~/.claude/agents/<name>.md`) if it's a standing rule for one agent's role.
- **Promote to a skill** if it belongs to a workflow that only runs when invoked.
- **Turn into a hook** if it must hold every time and can be checked mechanically.
- **Merge** with another memory that says the same thing.
- **Delete** if it was a one-off, is stale, or is already covered.

A memory that repeats a rule already in a CLAUDE.md or agent file means the prose rule isn't working: say so and consider a hook or clearer wording instead of another copy.

Default to the narrowest place that fully covers the lesson. Every line in a CLAUDE.md or memory index costs context in every session, so lean toward merging and deleting.

Show only the memories you would change, grouped by action, one line each with its location and the reason. Then one line for how many stay as they are. Wait for my input before changing anything. After we agree, apply the changes. When a lesson is promoted, delete the memory and its index line so it isn't loaded twice. Git history in `~/.claude` keeps a record of everything removed.
```

# Save session

- Kind: Claude Code skill
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/save-session/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/save-session/.

Saves where a project stands in a context file so the next session can pick up where this one left off.

- **What it is:** Save session is a Claude Code skill that writes a project's goal, decisions, and next steps into a context file at the end of a working session.
- **How it starts:** You type `/save-session`. Claude doesn't start it by itself.
- **Where the file goes:** `~/.claude/skills/save-session/SKILL.md`
- **Needs:** Nothing extra
- **To make it yours:** Put your own values where you see `<project-folder>`.
  Taken out for privacy: 1 private project folder pattern.

## The skill file (`SKILL.md`)

The instructions for saving a project's context at the end of a working session. It tells Claude how to find the project folder and write or update a context file there.

````
---
name: save-session
description: Save project context at end of a working session for continuity in future sessions
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash
---

# Save Session Context

Review the full conversation and save a structured context file so a future session can pick up where this one left off.

## Determine the project folder

Identify the project the user has been working on this session. Look at:
- The files that were read, edited, or created during the conversation
- The working directory and any directory changes
- The user's explicit mentions of a project name or folder

The project folder is the root directory of whatever project the user was working on (e.g., `~/ai/projects/<area>/<project-folder>/`, `~/ai/tools/<tool>/`). If you cannot confidently determine the project folder, ask the user before proceeding.

## Write context.md

Create or update a `context.md` file in the root of the project folder.

Use this structure:

```markdown
---
name: [project name]
description: [one-line project description]
last-updated: [YYYY-MM-DD]
---

## Goal
[What Orlando wants from this project, in his words where you have them.]

## Constraints
[Rules he set for this project.]

## Current State
[What exists now. What was accomplished in the most recent session.]

## Key Decisions
[Important choices made and their reasoning. Accumulate these across sessions. Don't discard prior decisions unless they've been reversed.]

## Next Steps
[What to pick up next time, in priority order.]

## Open Questions
[Anything unresolved or needing input.]
```

## Rules

- If `context.md` already exists, read it first and merge. Don't overwrite prior decisions or context that's still relevant. Update the `last-updated` date.
- If this is the first time, create the file from scratch based on the conversation.
- Current State describes the project now. Rewrite it each time; don't stack dated updates.
- Before writing that something is done or not done, check the files. Don't rely on memory of the conversation.
- Be concise. This file is for an LLM to read at the start of a session, not a full history.
- Only include information that would actually help a future session. Skip ephemeral details.
- Do not include information that can be derived from the code, git history, or existing project files.
````

---

# Tune setup

- Kind: Claude Code skill
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/tune-setup/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/tune-setup/.

Researches current Anthropic guidance, updates a guidance file, and proposes specific improvements to a Claude Code setup.

- **What it is:** Tune setup is a Claude Code skill that checks a Claude Code setup against current Anthropic guidance and proposes ranked improvements without applying them.
- **How it starts:** You type `/tune-setup`. Claude doesn't start it by itself.
- **Where the file goes:** `~/.claude/skills/tune-setup/SKILL.md`, its other files beside it
- **Needs:** Nothing extra
- **To make it yours:** Put your own values where you see `<project-folder>`.
  Taken out for privacy: 1 project folder and 1 path.

**Works with:** [Process feedback](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/process-feedback/) and [Save session](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/save-session/).

## The skill file (`SKILL.md`)

The instructions for a skill that researches current Anthropic guidance, updates one knowledge file, reviews the setup against it, and writes proposals for the owner to approve.

```
---
name: tune-setup
description: Research current Anthropic guidance on prompting and Claude Code, update the LLM guidance knowledge file, and propose specific improvements to agents, skills, and CLAUDE.md
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, WebSearch, WebFetch, Agent
---

# Tune Setup

Keep Orlando's Claude Code setup current with Anthropic's guidance. This skill replaces a dedicated "LLM Expert" agent: its knowledge lives in one file that only this skill reads, so other agents never pay for it in context.

Run it when a new Claude model or major Claude Code release ships, or when Orlando asks.

## 1. Load what we already know

Read `~/.claude/skills/tune-setup/llm-guidance.md`. If it doesn't exist, create it with the structure in step 3. Note the last-run date, which models it covered and the folder that holds that run's lookup; read that lookup and research only what's new since then.

For a full review, use `~/ai/projects/ai-setup/<project-folder>/` (in `ai-setup/zzCompleted/` once closed) as the pattern: parallel readers by area, a checker that tries to disprove each finding, and one page for Orlando.

## 2. Research

Use primary sources: Anthropic's docs (prompt engineering, model migration guides, Claude Code docs on memory and CLAUDE.md, skills, subagents, hooks, settings), Anthropic's engineering blog and news, and model release notes. Use secondary sources only to find primary ones.

- For broad runs, split research into parallel subagents by area (prompting, Claude Code features, model changes).
- Write what you find to `guidance.md` in this run's project folder (step 5), with the source URL and date for every finding.
- If a claim can't be traced to a primary source, mark it unverified. Never present a guess as guidance.

## 3. Update the knowledge file

`llm-guidance.md` keeps only what can't be looked up or measured again. Sections:

- **Last run:** date, current models, Claude Code version, and the path of this run's `guidance.md`.
- **Lessons from this setup:** what worked or didn't here, from feedback memories (see `/process-feedback`) and past audits in `~/ai/projects/ai-setup/`, plus setup decisions. Each decision gets its reason and a "revisit when" condition.

## 4. Check the setup against it

Review `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/ai/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/agents/`, `~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.claude/settings.json` (hooks included), the status line script, `~/ai/.claude/`, the vault's rules file, memory indexes and the memory files, agent memory (`~/.claude/agent-memory/`), and the tools in `~/ai/tools/`. Measure the size of everything that loads every session (CLAUDE.md files, memory indexes, model-invocable skill descriptions), since that's the recurring token cost.

Also:
- Challenge past decisions. For each entry in Lessons whose "revisit when" condition has been met, or that new guidance undercuts, propose keeping, changing or dropping it. Removing something that no longer earns its place counts as much as adding something.
- Re-check effort and model settings against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config. Settings can silently stop applying when a new model ships.
- Review memory as `~/.claude/skills/process-feedback/SKILL.md` describes, and put what it would change with the other proposals.
- If Orlando is at the Mac, ask him to run `/doctor prompt-audit`, `/skill-doctor`, `/context all`, and `/insights` and paste the output. They audit prompts for outdated patterns, show unused skills, list built-in features he isn't using, and measure the context this skill can't (system prompt, MCP tools, bundled skills).

## 5. Propose, don't apply

Write `~/ai/projects/ai-setup/<yyyymmdd>-tune-setup/proposals.md`: a short summary, then proposals ranked by value. For each: what to change (file and passage), why (with source), expected effect, and risk. Also write a `context.md` there (format in `~/.claude/skills/save-session/SKILL.md`). Make no changes until Orlando approves specific proposals. When every proposal is applied or decided, move the folder to `~/ai/projects/ai-setup/zzCompleted/`.

## Rules

- Plain language, no em dashes.
- Never put this material in `~/ai/CLAUDE.md` or workspace memory; every agent loads those.
- Say plainly when guidance conflicts with how Orlando likes to work, and let Orlando decide.
```

---

# Connect

- Kind: Claude Code skill
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/connect/
- Last updated: 2026-11-22

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/connect/.

Links new knowledge base notes to concept notes, builds concept notes for recurring ideas, and adds cross-area links.

- **What it is:** Connect is a Claude Code skill that links new or changed knowledge base notes to concept notes and to the rest of the vault.
- **How it starts:** You type `/connect`. Claude can also pick it up when it fits.
- **Where the file goes:** `~/.claude/skills/connect/SKILL.md`
- **Needs:** uv
- **To make it yours:** Put your own values where you see `<area>` and `<note>`.
  Taken out for privacy: 3 paths, 1 list of private folders, and 2 names.

**Works with:** [Close shop](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/close-shop/).

## The skill file (`SKILL.md`)

The instructions for connecting new notes in a knowledge base to the ideas they discuss. It is used after notes are added, or when asked to link a subject.

````
---
name: connect
description: Connect new or changed knowledge base notes to concepts and to the rest of the vault. Links notes to concept notes, adds them as sources, creates concept notes for ideas that now recur across sources, and adds cross-area links. Use after adding notes to ~/ai/knowledge-base (close-shop calls it), or when Orlando asks to connect, link or build concepts for a subject.
---

# Connect

The knowledge base stays useful to future agents only if what comes in gets connected: a new book, lecture or post should reach the ideas it discusses, and each idea should gather every source on it. This skill does that work. `kb.py connect` finds it; you judge it.

Read `~/ai/knowledge-base/AGENTS.md` first. Its rules on names, frontmatter, links and writing apply to everything here.

## Scope

- **After adding notes:** the notes you added or changed, plus their subject folders.
- **On demand:** a subject, such as `learning/<subject>`.

Run `uv run ~/ai/tools/scripts/kb.py connect --path <prefix>`. It lists three kinds of work:

1. **Names a concept without linking it:** a note uses a concept's name or alias in its text (quotes, Kindle highlights and headings don't count: links never go there).
2. **Topic in 2+ notes with no concept note:** a `topics:` value shared by several notes. These are candidates, not orders.
3. **No concept links to it:** in subjects that have concept notes, notes that no concept cites yet.

## 1. Link existing concepts

For each unlinked mention, open the note. Where the text uses the term in the concept's sense, even briefly, link the first mention in the body. Leave it unlinked only for another sense of the word, a title, or a place links can't go. Change only the link syntax, never Orlando's wording: `customer segmentation` becomes `[[market-segmentation|customer segmentation]]`.

Do this with `uv run ~/ai/tools/scripts/link_mentions.py propose ~/ai/tmp/links-<subject>-<time>.md --path <prefix>`: it lists each unlinked mention with every place a link can go, in context, and the words that matched. Write one decision per entry in a text file (`12: 1` links place 1, `13: no <reason>` leaves it), then run `link_mentions.py apply ~/ai/tmp/links-<subject>-<time>.json <decisions file>`, which adds link syntax only. Give each run a file name of its own like this one, so two runs at once never apply one run's decisions to the other's proposals. Every "no" goes to the vault's `_meta/connect-ignore.md` as judged not the concept (another sense, a title, a quote, no place), with its reason and those words, so `kb.py connect` stops listing that pair until the note matches a new word. Read all of an entry's places before a "no": it covers every listed place, and only the words recorded. A mention you judge without the script gets a line there by hand.

For each note in scope, find the concepts it discusses (its `topics`, and the concept names in its subject's `concepts/` folder). Link them at the first mention, and add the note to each concept note (step 3).

## 2. Decide which candidates become concept notes

Create a concept note when all of these hold:

- It's one idea: a framework, method, principle, model or measure. Not a company, a person, a case, a course or a whole field.
- At least two sources discuss it in substance, not in passing. The topic count is the starting signal; open the sources to confirm.
- Someone asking "what does Orlando know about X?" would want these sources brought together.

Skip the rest. People get notes in `people/` (see AGENTS.md), not concepts. When two candidates are the same idea under different names ("market segmentation", "customer segmentation"), make one concept with the other as an alias. When a candidate is a narrow case of an existing concept, add it as an alias or a line in that concept instead of a new note.

A large subject can have hundreds of candidates. Work from the top (most shared) down, and stop when the remaining ones are entities or one-off mentions. The leftover list is a backlog, not an error.

## 3. Write or update a concept note

- **Where:** `learning/<subject>/concepts/<name>.md`, in the subject where the idea is most at home. Sources from other subjects link in.
- **Name:** the idea's standard name, lowercase-kebab, unique across the vault (`find ~/ai/knowledge-base/ -iname "<name>.*"`).
- **Template:** `~/ai/knowledge-base/_meta/templates/concept.md`.
- **Frontmatter:** `type: concept`, `subject`, `summary`, `source: "Synthesized from the notes listed in sources"`, `sources` (a list of quoted links to every source note), and `aliases`. Aliases are what `kb.py connect` matches in other notes, so use specific phrases the sources actually use, six or more characters, never single common words like "trust" or "power". A shorter all-caps abbreviation the sources use for the whole idea ("NPV", "BATNA") or a short name with a capital letter ("Scrum") also works: it matches only as written (an abbreviation also as "NPVs" and in "NPV-based"). The title is usually the first alias, so a short capitalized title ("Lean") matches as written too, sentence starts included. To stop that, keep it out of `aliases` and put it in `title:` instead, as `flow-state` does with "Flow".
- **Body:**
  1. What the idea is, in a sentence or two, then how it works and when it applies. Build it only from the sources. No facts from your own knowledge; mark gaps `[?]`.
  2. `## Where it comes up`: one bullet per source: a link to the most specific place (a highlight block `[[<note>#^loc-1469]]`, a heading `[[<note>#Targeting]]`, or the note) and a sentence on what that source adds. Where sources disagree, say so. Quote at most a short phrase; the full quotes stay in the source notes.
  3. `## Related`: broader, narrower and opposing concepts, linked.
- **Updating an existing concept:** add the new source to `sources` and to "Where it comes up", and revise the explanation if the source adds something. Keep what's there.

## 4. Cross-area links

The graph is only as connected as the links across areas. For the notes in scope, search Orlando's writing and career for the same book, author or idea:

```
grep -rli "<distinctive phrase>\|<author surname>" ~/ai/knowledge-base/writing/blog/archive ~/ai/knowledge-base/<area> ~/ai/knowledge-base/<area> ~/ai/knowledge-base/<area>
```

Link both ways at the first mention, when the connection is real. A blog post reviewing a book, a career story that used a framework, a person who taught a course.

- Don't edit blog drafts in `writing/blog/` outside `archive/`: the publish script reads them.
- [A list of private folders is left out here.]

## 5. Finish

1. `uv run ~/ai/tools/scripts/kb.py hubs --path <subject>`: a new `concepts/` folder is listed in the subject's hub.
2. `uv run ~/ai/tools/scripts/kb.py check --path <prefix>`: fix what you introduced.
3. `uv run ~/ai/tools/scripts/kb.py connect --path <prefix>`: "names a concept without linking it" should be empty for your scope (mentions you judged not the concept are on the ignore list).
4. Say in a few lines what you did: concepts created and updated, links added, and any candidate you deliberately skipped that someone might expect.

## Working in parallel

For a big subject, agents can split the candidates, but only one agent edits a given concept note or a given source note at a time. Give each agent its own list of concepts, and collect links into other agents' notes in a report for one agent to apply.
````

---

# Obsidian to Hugo

- Kind: Claude Code skill
- Address: https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/obsidian-to-hugo/
- Last updated: 2026-11-23

> AI-written and cleaned from one person's working setup. Placeholders in angle brackets are not real values: ask your user for theirs. The newest version is at https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/obsidian-to-hugo/.

Converts an Obsidian blog post to Hugo-ready Markdown, fixes links and pictures, and places it in a review folder.

- **What it is:** Obsidian to Hugo is a Claude Code skill that converts a blog post written in Obsidian into Hugo-compatible Markdown and places it in a folder for review.
- **How it starts:** You type `/obsidian-to-hugo`. Claude can also pick it up when it fits.
- **Where the file goes:** `~/.claude/skills/obsidian-to-hugo/SKILL.md`, its other files beside it
- **Needs:** uv, Obsidian, and Hugo
- **To make it yours:** Put your own values where you see `<blog-folder>`, `<vault-folder>`, and `<yyyymmdd>`.
  Taken out for privacy: 4 paths, 1 blog folder name, and 6 dated project folder names.

This skill is specific to Orlando's blog. It is here because it is part of his setup, and its steps may still be worth borrowing.

**Works with:** [Corillo](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/apps/#corillo), [Relay](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/skills/relay/), and [Writer](https://oneillo.com/ai-setup/agents/writer/).

## The skill file (`SKILL.md`)

The instructions for the skill that converts an Obsidian blog post to Hugo Markdown. It is used when a post is ready to move from the notes vault to review.

````
---
name: obsidian-to-hugo
description: Convert an Obsidian blog post to Hugo-compatible markdown and place it in the blog projects folder for review
allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, AskUserQuestion
---

# Obsidian to Hugo Converter

Convert a blog post written in Obsidian to Hugo-compatible markdown and place it in `~/ai/projects/blog/` for editing and review.

## Paths

- **Obsidian source**: `<vault-folder>/writing/blog/`
- **Destination**: `~/ai/projects/blog/posts-to-review/`

If the Obsidian path does not exist, ask the user for the correct vault location.

## Steps

### 1. Identify the source file

If the user specified a filename (as an argument or in conversation), use that. Otherwise, list the markdown files in the Obsidian source directory and ask which one to convert.

Match flexibly -- the user might give a partial name, a slug, or a title. Find the closest match in the source directory.

### 2. Run the conversion

Run the conversion script:

```bash
uv run ~/.claude/skills/obsidian-to-hugo/scripts/convert.py --file "<filename>" [--verbose]
```

Run it without asking. If it says the converted file already exists, ask before running again with `--force`: the copy may hold review edits. The script does not modify the original Obsidian file.

A `[[link]]` becomes a link only when the post exists in `<blog-folder>/content/posts/`; any other link (a note, a heading) is kept as text without a link, with a warning. Pictures, both `![[...]]` embeds and standard links such as Corillo's, are copied next to the converted post.

Tests: `uv run --offline ~/.claude/skills/obsidian-to-hugo/scripts/test_convert.py`.

### 3. Report the result

After the script completes successfully, tell the user where the converted file landed. One line is enough. Example:

> Converted to `~/ai/projects/blog/posts-to-review/my-post-title/my-post-title.md`

If the script reported any warnings (missing images, links kept as text), relay those.

### 4. Errors

If the script fails, show the error output and suggest a fix. Common issues:
- Source file not found -- check the filename and list available files
- Destination directory missing -- this shouldn't happen, but create it if needed
````

## Scripts

These scripts are one person's working code, shared from Orlando's setup with private details replaced by placeholders. They are not a supported tool: read each one before you run it, and expect to change it to fit your own setup.

### `convert.py`

The script that turns an Obsidian post into Hugo Markdown. It rewrites picture embeds and links to other posts, copies the pictures, and saves the result in the review folder without touching the original.

**Needs to run:** uv.

````
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.12"
# dependencies = []
# ///
"""
Obsidian to Hugo Converter

Converts Obsidian-native markdown to Hugo-compatible markdown and places
the result in ~/ai/projects/blog/posts-to-review/ for review with the writer agent.

Does NOT modify the original Obsidian file.
"""

import argparse
import re
import shutil
import sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import quote, unquote

# Default paths (macOS Obsidian vault)
DEFAULT_SOURCE = (
    Path.home()
    / "<vault-folder>/writing/blog"
)
DEFAULT_DEST = Path.home() / "ai/projects/blog/posts-to-review"
DEFAULT_BLOG = Path.home() / "<blog-folder>/content/posts"

# Obsidian's size suffix on an embed: |400 or |400x300
SIZE_ONLY = re.compile(r"^\d+(x\d+)?$")


def slugify(title: str) -> str:
    """Convert a post title to a Hugo-compatible slug.

    'My Great Post' -> 'my-great-post'
    '<yyyymmdd>-my-post' -> 'my-post'
    """
    slug = title.lower().strip()
    # Strip leading date prefix (YYYYMMDD- or YYYY-MM-DD-)
    slug = re.sub(r"^\d{4}-?\d{2}-?\d{2}-", "", slug)
    slug = re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]", "", slug)  # Remove special chars
    slug = re.sub(r"[\s_]+", "-", slug)  # Spaces/underscores to hyphens
    slug = re.sub(r"-+", "-", slug)  # Collapse multiple hyphens
    slug = slug.strip("-")
    return slug


def find_code_regions(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Find all code block and inline code regions to skip during transforms."""
    regions = []
    # Fenced code blocks
    for match in re.finditer(r"```[\s\S]*?```", text):
        regions.append((match.start(), match.end()))
    # Inline code spans
    for match in re.finditer(r"`[^`]+`", text):
        regions.append((match.start(), match.end()))
    return regions


def in_protected_region(pos: int, regions: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> bool:
    """Check if a position falls inside a protected region."""
    return any(start <= pos < end for start, end in regions)


def find_frontmatter_end(text: str) -> int:
    """Find the end position of YAML frontmatter (if present).

    Returns 0 if no frontmatter found.
    """
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return 0
    match = re.match(r"^---\s*\n.*?\n---\s*\n", text, re.DOTALL)
    return match.end() if match else 0


def transform_image_embeds(
    text: str, code_regions: list[tuple[int, int]], fm_end: int
) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """Convert Obsidian image embeds and local picture links to standard markdown.

    ![[image.png]]          -> ![](image.png)
    ![[image.png|alt text]] -> ![alt text](image.png)
    ![[image.png|400]]      -> ![](image.png)          (size dropped)
    ![[Pasted image.png]]   -> ![](Pasted%20image.png)
    ![Chart](post%20images/chart.png) -> ![Chart](chart.png)   (Corillo's form)

    Every picture ends up next to the post, so links use the bare, encoded name.
    Returns (transformed_text, list_of_referenced_images), where each image is
    its path relative to the source file, decoded.
    """
    images = []
    embed = re.compile(r"!\[\[([^\]|]+?)(?:\|([^\]]*))?\]\]")
    # Standard picture links to local files (not web addresses)
    standard = re.compile(r"!\[([^\]]*)\]\((?![a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*:)([^)\s]+)\)")

    def skip(match):
        return in_protected_region(match.start(), code_regions) or match.start() < fm_end

    def link(alt: str, path: str) -> str:
        images.append(path)
        return f"![{alt}]({quote(Path(path).name)})"

    def replace_embed(match):
        if skip(match):
            return match.group(0)
        alt = match.group(2).strip() if match.group(2) else ""
        if SIZE_ONLY.match(alt):
            alt = ""
        return link(alt, match.group(1).strip())

    def replace_standard(match):
        if skip(match):
            return match.group(0)
        return link(match.group(1), unquote(match.group(2)))

    # Standard links first: embed output is itself a standard link.
    text = standard.sub(replace_standard, text)
    code_regions = find_code_regions(text)
    fm_end = find_frontmatter_end(text)
    return embed.sub(replace_embed, text), images


def post_exists(blog_dir: Path, slug: str) -> bool:
    """True if the blog has a post at this slug (bundle folder or single file)."""
    return bool(slug) and (
        (blog_dir / slug).is_dir() or (blog_dir / f"{slug}.md").is_file()
    )


def transform_wikilinks(
    text: str, code_regions: list[tuple[int, int]], fm_end: int, blog_dir: Path
) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """Convert Obsidian wikilinks to Hugo ref links, only for posts that exist.

    [[Post Title]]              -> [Post Title]({{< ref "post-title" >}})
    [[Post Title|Display Text]] -> [Display Text]({{< ref "post-title" >}})
    [[Post Title#Heading]]      -> same as [[Post Title]] (heading dropped)

    A link to anything that is not a published post (a note, a heading in this
    post) would stop the Hugo build, so it becomes its display text with no
    link. Returns (transformed_text, warnings).
    """
    pattern = re.compile(r"(?<!!)\[\[([^\]|]+?)(?:\|([^\]]*))?\]\]")
    warnings = []

    def replace(match):
        if in_protected_region(match.start(), code_regions) or match.start() < fm_end:
            return match.group(0)
        target = match.group(1).strip()
        page, _, heading = target.partition("#")
        page = page.strip()
        display = match.group(2).strip() if match.group(2) else (
            page or heading.lstrip("^").strip()
        )
        slug = slugify(page)
        if post_exists(blog_dir, slug):
            return f'[{display}]({{{{< ref "{slug}" >}}}})'
        warnings.append(
            f"link {match.group(0)} is not a post on the blog; kept the text without a link"
        )
        return display

    return pattern.sub(replace, text), warnings


def convert_post(
    content: str, blog_dir: Path = DEFAULT_BLOG
) -> tuple[str, list[str], list[str]]:
    """Apply all transforms to a post's content.

    Returns (converted_content, list_of_referenced_images, link_warnings).
    """
    fm_end = find_frontmatter_end(content)
    code_regions = find_code_regions(content)

    # Image embeds first (changes positions, so recalculate after)
    content, images = transform_image_embeds(content, code_regions, fm_end)

    # Recalculate protected regions after image transform
    code_regions = find_code_regions(content)
    fm_end = find_frontmatter_end(content)

    content, warnings = transform_wikilinks(content, code_regions, fm_end, blog_dir)

    return content, images, warnings


def process_file(
    source_file: Path,
    source_dir: Path,
    dest_dir: Path,
    blog_dir: Path = DEFAULT_BLOG,
    verbose: bool = False,
    force: bool = False,
) -> Path:
    """Process a single markdown file. Returns the output file path."""
    slug = slugify(source_file.stem)
    project_dir = dest_dir / slug
    out_file = project_dir / f"{slug}.md"
    if out_file.exists() and not force:
        print(
            f"Error: {out_file} already exists and may hold review edits. "
            "Run again with --force to replace it.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(1)

    content = source_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    converted, images, warnings = convert_post(content, blog_dir)

    project_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_file.write_text(converted, encoding="utf-8")

    if not blog_dir.is_dir():
        print(f"  Warning: blog posts folder not found: {blog_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
    for warning in warnings:
        print(f"  Warning: {warning}", file=sys.stderr)

    if verbose:
        print(f"  Source:  {source_file}")
        print(f"  Output:  {out_file}")
        if images:
            print(f"  Images:  {', '.join(images)}")

    # Copy referenced images
    for img_name in images:
        img_source = source_file.parent / img_name
        if img_source.is_file():
            img_dest = project_dir / Path(img_name).name
            shutil.copy2(img_source, img_dest)
            if verbose:
                print(f"  Copied image: {img_name}")
        else:
            print(f"  Warning: image not found: {img_source}", file=sys.stderr)

    return out_file


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Convert Obsidian markdown to Hugo-compatible format"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--source",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_SOURCE,
        help=f"Obsidian blog directory (default: {DEFAULT_SOURCE})",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dest",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_DEST,
        help=f"Destination directory (default: {DEFAULT_DEST})",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--blog",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_BLOG,
        help=f"Blog posts folder, to check that linked posts exist (default: {DEFAULT_BLOG})",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--force",
        action="store_true",
        help="Replace an existing converted copy (it may hold review edits)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--file",
        type=str,
        required=True,
        help="Filename to convert (relative to source dir)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Print detailed conversion info",
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Validate source directory
    if not args.source.exists():
        print(f"Error: Source directory not found: {args.source}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Use --source to specify your Obsidian vault path.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Validate destination directory
    if not args.dest.exists():
        print(f"Error: Destination directory not found: {args.dest}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Find the source file -- check root, then search subdirectories
    source_file = args.source / args.file
    if not source_file.is_file() and not args.file.endswith(".md"):
        source_file = args.source / f"{args.file}.md"
    if not source_file.is_file():
        # Search subdirectories for a matching .md file
        name = args.file if args.file.endswith(".md") else f"{args.file}.md"
        matches = sorted(args.source.glob(f"*/{name}"))
        if matches:
            source_file = matches[0]
    if not source_file.is_file():
        print(f"Error: File not found: {source_file}", file=sys.stderr)
        # List available files as a hint (root + one level deep)
        md_files = sorted(args.source.glob("*.md")) + sorted(
            args.source.glob("*/*.md")
        )
        if md_files:
            print("\nAvailable files:", file=sys.stderr)
            for f in md_files:
                rel = f.relative_to(args.source)
                print(f"  {rel}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    out_file = process_file(
        source_file, args.source, args.dest, args.blog, args.verbose, args.force
    )
    print(f"Converted to {out_file}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````

### `test_convert.py`

The tests for the conversion script, run on made-up posts in a temporary folder. They check links, pictures, the guard against overwriting review edits, and file name matching.

**Needs to run:** uv.

```
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.12"
# ///
"""Tests for convert.py, on made-up posts in a temp folder.

Run: uv run --offline test_convert.py [path/to/convert.py]
"""

import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT = Path(sys.argv.pop(1) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path(__file__).with_name("convert.py"))


class ConvertTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.src, self.dest, self.blog = root / "src", root / "dest", root / "posts"
        for d in (self.src, self.dest, self.blog):
            d.mkdir()
        (self.blog / "soil-basics").mkdir()
        (self.blog / "another-post.md").write_text("x")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def run_convert(self, name, *extra):
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(SCRIPT), "--source", str(self.src), "--dest", str(self.dest),
             "--blog", str(self.blog), "--file", name, *extra],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        )

    def post(self, body, folder="test-post"):
        d = self.src / folder
        d.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (d / f"{folder}.md").write_text(body)
        return d

    def out(self):
        return (self.dest / "test-post" / "test-post.md").read_text()

    def test_links_only_to_existing_posts(self):  # L3
        self.post("[[soil-basics|earlier post]], [[market-segmentation|segments]], "
                  "[[Another Post#Part two]], [[the-dirt-book#^loc-200]], [[#Wrap up]].\n")
        r = self.run_convert("test-post.md")
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.out(), '[earlier post]({{< ref "soil-basics" >}}), segments, '
                         '[Another Post]({{< ref "another-post" >}}), the-dirt-book, Wrap up.\n')
        self.assertEqual(r.stderr.count("not a post on the blog"), 3)

    def test_pictures(self):  # L4
        d = self.post("![[Pasted image 2026.png]] ![[chart.png|400]] ![[plan.png|the plan]]\n"
                      "![Chart](test-post%20images/corillo-chart.png) ![Gone](missing.png) "
                      "![Video](https://youtu.be/abc)\n")
        for name in ("Pasted image 2026.png", "chart.png", "plan.png"):
            (d / name).write_bytes(b"img")
        (d / "test-post images").mkdir()
        (d / "test-post images" / "corillo-chart.png").write_bytes(b"img")
        r = self.run_convert("test-post.md")
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.out(), "![](Pasted%20image%202026.png) ![](chart.png) ![the plan](plan.png)\n"
                         "![Chart](corillo-chart.png) ![Gone](missing.png) ![Video](https://youtu.be/abc)\n")
        for name in ("Pasted image 2026.png", "chart.png", "plan.png", "corillo-chart.png"):
            self.assertTrue((self.dest / "test-post" / name).is_file(), name)
        self.assertIn("image not found", r.stderr)
        self.assertIn("missing.png", r.stderr)

    def test_second_run_keeps_review_edits(self):  # L5
        self.post("Hello.\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_convert("test-post.md").returncode, 0)
        out = self.dest / "test-post" / "test-post.md"
        out.write_text("Hello, edited.\n")
        r = self.run_convert("test-post.md")
        self.assertNotEqual(r.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("--force", r.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(out.read_text(), "Hello, edited.\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_convert("test-post.md", "--force").returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(out.read_text(), "Hello.\n")

    def test_name_without_md_and_same_named_folder(self):  # L19
        self.post("Hello.\n")
        r = self.run_convert("test-post")
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.out(), "Hello.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```
